summary.note: Cumulative structural challenge closure for the persisted b03 frontier. No fresh ordinary companies opened because downstream ready backlog is above target. Underwriting gaps remain owned by Alpha/Deep/machine and are not converted into Beta blockers.

claims: Test intensity is the causal capture point between rising compute complexity and deployable silicon; TER is exposed to that bottleneck but not guaranteed to capture all incremental test spend.
contradictions: AI demand can strengthen while TER capture weakens
evidence.falsifier: AI/memory unit complexity and volumes rise materially while TER test demand/capture persistently decouples

claims: Automation demand addresses labor/productivity constraints, but ROK value capture depends on control/software integration and customer capex rather than automation demand alone.
contradictions: secular automation can coexist with cyclical organic weakness
evidence.falsifier: automation capex expands across served markets while ROK organic demand persistently decouples

claims: ADAS adoption creates perception/compute demand, but OEM qualification and design-win retention are the successor bottlenecks controlling MBLY capture.
contradictions: ADAS category growth does not guarantee MBLY share retention
evidence.falsifier: ADAS penetration rises while MBLY design wins and production volumes structurally erode

claims: Autonomous last-mile delivery can relieve labor/cost constraints, but fleet density and positive unit economics are successor bottlenecks.
contradictions: deployment/revenue growth can increase without proving economic viability
evidence.falsifier: fleet deployment scales materially without a credible path to positive gross economics

claims: Autonomous trucking targets freight labor/utilization constraints; certification, network access, commercial miles and self-funding economics form sequential successor bottlenecks.
contradictions: technical milestones do not establish self-funding economics
evidence.falsifier: technical/regulatory access advances while commercial miles and economic conversion fail persistently

claims: Electrification and data-center load stress grid distribution, making electrical equipment capacity a bottleneck; ETN capture depends on backlog conversion and execution through acquisition/separation complexity.
contradictions: secular demand can coexist with leverage and integration risk
evidence.falsifier: grid/data-center infrastructure spending expands while ETN electrical backlog and conversion structurally contract

claims: Grid/data-center buildout shifts the bottleneck from equipment availability to engineering/construction execution; PWR capture depends on award/RPO conversion and project discipline.
contradictions: large backlog does not guarantee margin or cash conversion
evidence.falsifier: infrastructure commitments remain strong while PWR awards/RPO conversion and normalized cash economics weaken

claims: High-density industrial/data-center power creates distribution and switchgear/control bottlenecks; POWL benefits only while order conversion and project execution remain disciplined.
contradictions: mega-orders strengthen demand visibility while increasing concentration/schedule fragility
evidence.falsifier: served electrical demand expands while POWL order/backlog conversion persistently deteriorates

claims: Firm-power demand meets generation/interconnection scarcity; fleet availability, licensing and contract economics are successor bottlenecks controlling CEG capture.
contradictions: license applications and scarcity are not completed approvals or guaranteed economics
evidence.falsifier: firm-power scarcity persists while CEG contracted fleet utilization/economics structurally weaken

claims: Load growth and dispatchable scarcity support integrated generation/retail value, but hedge realization and fleet cash generation determine durable capture.
contradictions: hedging dampens near-term volatility but cannot remove structural commodity exposure
evidence.falsifier: load/scarcity rises while normalized VST fleet cash generation structurally deteriorates

claims: Power/interconnection scarcity can shift data-center demand toward onsite resilient generation; BE capture depends on deployment economics, margins and customer diversification.
contradictions: rapid growth need not equal diversified durable demand
evidence.falsifier: power scarcity persists while BE deployment growth and normalized margins fail structurally

claims: Firm clean-power demand can create a nuclear-development bottleneck, but licensing is only an intermediate gate; binding financed projects and delivered economics are successor bottlenecks.
contradictions: certification/framework progress does not equal binding financed deployment
evidence.falsifier: licensing/framework progress fails persistently to convert into binding financed projects
